answer.rationale: Three problems compete for the single experiment slot: competitor price pressure on SMB, and declines in both activation and onboarding completion. Promotional pricing (memory_73) directly counters the competitor but risks a margin/quality race-to-the-bottom that the memory itself doesn't validate against retention or long-term qualified revenue (unlike memory_57's referral finding, which explicitly checked retention impact). Given the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue rather than short-term share defense, I favor addressing the onboarding completion decline directly, which has durable prior support from both memory_31 (signup simplification lifting SMB activation) and memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value). Before committing, I want to verify these two records since the decision rests on their reliability and I want to confirm they didn't trade completion/speed for lead quality or downstream retention, which would itself pose a hidden value risk. This leaves the competitor pricing threat and activation messaging unaddressed this cycle — an explicit, acknowledged tradeoff rather than a resolved one. Scale is set to a standard experiment rather than broad rollout given competing priorities and unverified downstream effects on account quality.
